newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 10.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:

* "Star Wars" by News Corp's Twentieth Century Fox grossed $22.8 million over the weekend, according to studio estimates. Meanwhile, "Dante's Peak" by Seagram Co Ltd's Universal, grossed $18.6 million, a record for a February opening. Ticket sales for all $500,000-plus grossers totaled about $76 million, 23 percent above the equivalent weekend last year. Together, "Star Wars" and "Dante's Peak" accounted for more than half of the weekend total.

* Hasbro and Lewis Galoob Toys currently share rights to the "Star Wars" toy line, which has sold an estimated $2 billion at retail and is expected to generate $500 million more this year. But Lucasfilm, which produced the trilogy and controls merchandising rights, has invited giants Mattel and Playmates Toys, sources said, to try to boost the upfront payment it collects for granting rights to the film's characters.

* B-movie king Roger Corman and his wife Julie Corman have a deal to sell their 14-year-old film production and video company Concorde-New Horizons to veteran producer Elliot Kastner. Due to close May 1, the deal announced Friday -- worth $100 million, sources said -- gives Kastner the studio's ongoing operations, including the 378-title feature film library, the production facility in Venice and its Brentwood headquarters, as well as several other Los Angeles buildings and related investments.

* After a year as a William Morris client, Sylvester Stallone has left the agency and will now be represented by Creative Artists Agency's Fred Specktor, who represented Stallone when the actor was first starting out some 20 years ago.

* Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott has asked President Clinton to nominate House Commerce Committee chief economist Harold Furchtgott-Roth as the next Republican Federal Communications Commission commissioner.

* Sony Corp's Columbia TriStar Television has a two-year, multimillion-dollar deal with writer-producer Jeff Franklin, who is currently executive producing the Columbia TriStar UPN comedy "Malcolm & Eddie."
